free_tier.stated: [translated] 'A free service, designed for users who do not have a public IP.' 'It supports both TCP and UDP traffic forwarding at the same time, ensuring stable server operation.'

egress.terms: [translated] No byte allowance, rate or session length is published on the front page, the how-to page, the terms page or the client download page. The only limit visible is an account expiry, which the status panel reports.; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: the downloads page lists per-architecture binaries and a separate FRPC file.
tooling: the vendor's client builds for Windows 386/amd64/arm64, Linux on 11 architectures, macOS two builds, version 1.1.1; a custom FRPC file is also offered
chaining: A Taiwanese UDP port forward is the missing third leg of an Asia set that already covers Japan and Korea, and it needs no phone number.

limits.value: [translated] 'The account has already expired, the proxy cannot be started! Please contact TaiwanFRP.'

binding_note: No byte allowance is published anywhere, so no volume quota can be shown to fail first. What the site itself displays as a failure is an expired account: the status panel reports the expiry and refuses to start the proxy.

identity_cost.detail: [translated] Registration takes a username, a password and a verification code obtained from the vendor's Discord: 'one Discord user may register only one account'. The third field reads 'Taiwan mobile phone (not required) - Taiwan mobile numbers only, landlines cannot be used; some features require a phone number, which you can also add later in the account settings'.

reliability_note: Nodes provided by other users are described by the vendor as sometimes unstable; the account expiry stops the proxy; Discord membership is checked at start-up.
confidence_note: Ingress is documented (TCP and UDP on a public port, no public IP needed) and identity is documented (Discord code, phone optional). The volume is absent from every page read, so the verdict rests on a dimension that was never measured.

notes: The only Taiwanese free service found that forwards UDP on a public port without a public IP, and the cheapest identity cost: a Discord account, with the Taiwanese mobile number explicitly optional and needed only for some features. Two gaps. Every page is silent on volume. And the account appears to carry an expiry a user must renew, which the status panel reports as a hard stop. Country: Taiwan; the operator writes in Traditional Chinese, and the terms invoke the law of the Republic of China. A user is frp-based: a 'custom client FRPC file' is offered for download.

extras.wg_detail: [translated] 'Register an account and create a proxy, and you can host a Minecraft or other TCP/UDP server.' A UDP proxy on a public port would carry a WireGuard datagram; the vendor issues no .conf and a user is their own build.
extras.volume_stated: [translated] No byte allowance, rate or session length is published on the front page, the how-to page, the terms page or the client download page. The only limit visible is an account expiry, which the status panel reports.
extras.transit_note: The vendor's Taiwanese public node relays to the client's machine.
